paragraphs.text: A recruiter once asked me why I was applying for non-tech roles when my internships were in Data Analytics and AI & Machine Learning. I had to explain that I was actually a BBA graduate. It made me realise how far I had moved from my academic starting point without really noticing it.

My degree is in business, but my internships took me into data, AI, research, writing and digital operations. Across all of them, I found myself doing the same things: **finding information, checking it carefully, making sense of it, and explaining what I found.** That's the kind of work I enjoy.

I approach most things the same way: **find out what it is, understand how it works, then do it step by step.** I'm curious by habit. I always end up in the comment section, searching for whatever caught my eye, and that's how I found Power BI and SQL after working with Python in one internship. I prefer figuring things out one step at a time, but when something matters, **I give it everything**. I work best independently within a clear framework, so I know what I'm doing and what I'm accountable for.

cards.title: The Process
cards.text: I research before I act, work systematically, and document everything. I don't skip steps and I don't guess when I can verify.

cards.title: The Detail
cards.text: I notice inconsistencies. Whether it's a dataset with placeholder dates disguised as values, or a brief that contradicts itself, I tend to stop and check it.

cards.title: The Range
cards.text: Business degree, data internships. I can speak both languages, so I can sit in either room and make sense of what's happening.
